findings.description: The security group allows inbound TCP/22 from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing SSH on the instance to the entire internet and enabling brute-force or exploit attempts.
The egress rule permits all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0, allowing a compromised host unrestricted outbound connections for data exfiltration or C2 traffic.

findings.issue_category: hardcoded cloud credentials in user data
findings.description: The user_data script exports AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY as plaintext literals; EC2 user data is retrievable from the instance metadata service by any process/user on the host and is stored unencrypted in the instance description.
No metadata_options block requiring http_tokens = "required" is set, so IMDSv1 remains enabled and SSRF on the web server could be used to read instance metadata and credentials.
The instance does not configure root_block_device with encrypted = true, so the root EBS volume may store data at rest unencrypted.
The instance launches in a subnet with map_public_ip_on_launch = true combined with a wide-open security group, placing it directly on the internet with no NAT or load balancer in front.
The EBS volume is created without encrypted = true and no KMS key, so data written to the attached disk is stored unencrypted.
The snapshot derives from an unencrypted volume, so backup data is stored unencrypted and could be exposed if snapshot permissions are ever loosened.
The VPC flow log bucket has no server-side encryption configuration (SSE-KMS/SSE-S3), leaving sensitive network telemetry unencrypted at rest.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block or ACL/policy controls are defined for the flow log bucket, so a future ACL or policy change could expose network flow records publicly.
Versioning is not enabled on the audit/flow-log bucket, so log objects can be overwritten or deleted without recovery, undermining forensic integrity.

findings.issue_category: force destroy enabled on log bucket
findings.description: force_destroy = true permits Terraform to delete the bucket and all stored flow logs without safeguards, allowing destruction of security audit evidence.
No bucket policy enforcing aws:SecureTransport is attached, so log data could be transmitted over unencrypted HTTP connections.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true causes every instance in this subnet to receive a public IP address, expanding internet-facing attack surface by default.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true causes every instance in this subnet to receive a public IP address, expanding internet-facing attack surface by default.
The VPC does not manage/restrict its default security group (no aws_default_security_group resource), so resources launched without an explicit SG inherit unrestricted intra-group access.
